zoe.sec: Notice: legacy long-lived service tokens and personal API tokens used by services and automation will be sunset. Date: enforcement 2026-11-15 00:00 UTC. Please migrate to scoped short-lived service-tokens or OIDC-based federation.

zoe.sec: Why: tokens with unlimited TTL are the largest contributor to escalations in our incident history. Scoped, attestable tokens reduce lateral movement and make revocation visible.

zoe.sec: Timeline:
- Today: announcement (migration guidance posted to Confluence)
- Discovery window: 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-14
- Migration window: 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-14
- Enforcement (deny at auth-proxy): 2026-11-15

zoe.sec: Actions for teams:
- Find tokens: `git grep -n "REDWOOD_API_TOKEN" || git grep -n "authorization: Bearer"`
- Replace usage with: service-token broker OR GitHub/GCP OIDC federation.
- Update CI/CD, cronjobs, and external integrations to call `POST /token-broker/v1/mint` and use returned token in-memory.

zoe.sec: Example curl (mint scoped token):
```
curl -X POST https://token-broker.internal/mint \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OIDC_ASSERTION" \
  -d '{"role":"deploy-agent","ttl":"3600s"}'
```

ops-bot: org-scan: scanned 780 repos 93 flagged 112 references to long-lived tokens, 39 plaintext tokens in vaults. CSV uploaded to #security-scans.

matt.dev: For external SaaS integrations (PagerDuty, Datadog) that only accept a static token, what do we do?

zoe.sec: Two options: 1) use a short-lived token via a small proxy that auto-rotates (recommended), or 2) request a scoped, low-priv TTL token from the vendor with documented rotation. Exceptions allowed for legacy vendors with mitigation (IP allowlist + quarterly rotation).

lia.sre: Will the enforcement block only new tokens or also existing ones on 11/15?

zoe.sec: Enforcement will deny tokens that are not minted by our token-broker or OIDC provider. Existing legacy tokens will stop working on 11/15 unless an approved exception exists.

tom.platform: We can add a migration helper to auto-detect bearer tokens in workflows and open PRs to replace with broker calls. I'll queue this under infra-automation.

zoe.sec: Awesome, thanks. If you're generating PRs, tag them `security:token-migration` so scans ignore in-flight changes.

marc.ciso: This aligns with audit recommendations. Team leads: escalate any blockers by 2026-10-20.

matt.dev: Small edge-case: some on-prem customer connectors can't reach the broker. How to get temporary access?

zoe.sec: For on-prem connectors, open an exception and supply network mitigations (mutual TLS, IP restrictions) and a TTL plan. Exceptions are short (max 30 days) and require an owner.

lia.sre: We'll prioritize SRE-owned automation and remove tokens from Vault in bulk where safe.

zoe.sec: Final: migration docs + token-broker SDKs and example PR templates are on Confluence now. Reach out in-thread for repo-specific help. Enforcement 2026-11-15. :lock:
